what_the_eye_sees: In the hero at 300 px you see a lizard wrapped round a plain polished band before you see anything else: a head at the top left, a beaded ridge down its back, a clawed foot gripping the band's edge, and a tail running off round the right. A jeweller would say 'lizard ring' at once, which is a pass for the block-out. They would not say tuatara. The animal reads at the level of 'lizard' (gecko, iguana or chameleon), not as this animal. Three things hold it there. (1) The head is decorated, not anatomical. The flanks of the head carry scroll or paisley curls like filigree, with no mouth line, no beak or overbite at the snout and no separate eye. So the peridot, which sits where an eye would be in the three-quarter view, reads as a big green eye. From the side the animal looks like a chameleon or a frog-eyed lizard, not a stone on the skull. (2) The dorsal ridge is a row of small round beads. It reads as a bead line or spine knuckles, not the tuatara's comb of separate triangular spines. In face-300 the body behind the head, with dense tubercles and a central ridge running to a point, reads as a pine cone, an arrowhead or a feather quill more than a back. (3) The limbs and tail break up. The hind foot at the lower left of the hero reads as a separate knob or bolt head on the band's edge, and the low crest on the right of the hero reads as a separate strip, not the continuation of one tapering tail. In face-300 the splayed front feet with toes help the read, and the stone sits cleanly centred on the head, but the head's rounded lozenge with curls on each side reads more as an ornament or a mask than a reptile's skull. Against the bar: Caiman and the Reptilia tiles read as specific hide at thumbnail size. This reads as a specific creature form, which is stronger, but it is not yet a specific animal.

changes.what: Model the head as a tuatara skull instead of an ornamented lozenge: add real eyes, and give the peridot the parietal position behind them so it stops reading as the eye.
changes.where: Head, t = 0 to 12.5 mm along the animal (width knots 0 to 3.4 mm; stone at t = 8.5 mm). Remove the scroll/curl relief on both head flanks.
changes.by_how_much: Two eyes (Logan allows eyes, 2026-09-24), one on each side of the head at about t = 5 to 6 mm: domed, about 1.3 mm across and 0.5 mm proud, each under a heavy brow ridge 0.3 to 0.4 mm proud. Move the stone back to t = 9.5 to 10 mm, on the midline behind and between the eyes. Cut a mouth line 0.3 mm deep from the snout tip back to below the eye, with a blunt downturned beak overhang of about 0.4 mm at the snout. Acceptance: in hero-300 two dark eye domes are visible and separate from the green stone, and the stone sits behind them on top of the skull. In face-300 the stone is visibly behind the line joining the eyes.

changes.what: Replace the beaded dorsal ridge with the tuatara's comb: separate triangular spines, tallest at the nape and over the shoulders, with a clear gap at the pelvis, then a lower saw down the tail.
changes.where: Crest along the midline from the back of the head (t about 12.5 mm) to the tail tip (t = 80 mm), following crest_knots.
changes.by_how_much: Spines with a triangular side profile, about 1.4 to 1.6 mm pitch, 0.9 to 1.2 mm tall at the nape and shoulders (t = 13 to 30 mm), dropping to 0.5 to 0.6 mm across the back. Leave a break of about 3 mm with no spines at the hips (t about 32 mm), then a 0.4 to 0.5 mm saw grading down to about 0.2 mm at the tail tip. Keep the spines at 0.8 mm or more at the base. Acceptance: in hero-300 the back shows a row of pointed teeth against the polished band, not round beads. In face-300 the silhouette behind the head reads as a spiny back, not a cone or arrowhead.

changes.what: Join the limbs and the tail into one continuous body.
changes.where: The hind foot at the lower left of the hero (palm-side edge), and the tail segment on the right of the hero (t about 45 to 80 mm).
changes.by_how_much: Give each hind limb a visible thigh, at least 1.5 mm thick, rising out of the body's flank to the foot, with five splayed toes about 0.5 mm wide, like the front feet. Make the tail one unbroken form that tapers smoothly along the width knots (2.25 to 0.6 mm) with no step or gap in its height, and carry the crest saw along it to the tip. Acceptance: in hero-300 no part of the animal reads as a separate knob or strip. The eye follows one outline from snout to tail tip, with four limbs attached to it.
